subject: More on the apple processing problem

messages.author: 32ca34ebc225cb13
messages.subject: More on the apple processing problem
parts:
I am still on the apple grading/sorting/packing process.  My question this time is on the front end of the process.

1. The apples are delivered in bins of ~4525 apples and they are tipped into a water bath.  They are then accumulated (queued) in the water bath and progressively conveyed into a washer.
2.  From the washer they are singulated, graded, sorted, packed and paletised [this was covered in the previous post which was handled really well using the Batch() function]

My question is:

1.  How do I handle the bins (do I use batch and separate??) when they are dumped?
2. How do I code the add_generator statement when I want 4525 apples to be dumped every 6 minutes into the water bath?

I know the answer is probably very straightforward, I just cannot think of a way forward

Regards
Stuart

On Tue, 19 Feb 2019 at 23:03, Stuart Dykes <sdyk...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I am still on the apple grading/sorting/packing process. My question this time is on the front end of the process.
>
> 1. The apples are delivered in bins of ~4525 apples and they are tipped into a water bath. They are then accumulated (queued) in the water bath and progressively conveyed into a washer.
> 2. From the washer they are singulated, graded, sorted, packed and paletised [this was covered in the previous post which was handled really well using the Batch() function]
>
> My question is:
>
> 1. How do I handle the bins (do I use batch and separate??) when they are dumped?
> 2. How do I code the add_generator statement when I want 4525 apples to be dumped every 6 minutes into the water bath?

If you use the simple generator "function() 1", one arrival is
generated every minute (if you are using minutes as the base time
unit). If you instead use "function() c(1, 0)", then one arrival is
generated in one minute and another one right afterwards (null
interarrival time), so 2 arrivals are generated every minute.
Therefore,

function() c(rnorm(1, 6), rep(0, rnorm(1, 4525)))

generates around 4525 arrivals approx. every 6 minutes. You can adjust
the standard deviations to fit your needs or even choose other
distributions.

Iñaki
